qc.label_under_test: The English word 'Mexican' (adjective or noun, any topic: food, people, government, animals), not 'Mexico', 'Mexicans', other-language forms (mexicana) or other nationality words such as Canadian, Indian or Japanese; Turkish and Spanish fire weakly, and brand names inside lists of companies (Marriott, Vivendi) also fire and are not tested here.

neighbours.label: The English word 'Mexican' in any context (strongest), and weaker, other nationality adjectives only when they open a company, airline or band name inside a comma-separated list (Turkish Airlines, Swedish House Mafia); the same adjectives in plain prose (the Swedish government), Canadian/Japanese/Indian, and 'Mexico' stay quiet.
fire: We ordered Mexican food for the whole office on Friday.
Her grandmother was Mexican and taught her to make tamales from scratch.
The museum opened a new wing devoted to Mexican muralists of the 1930s.
Mexican authorities announced the new border crossing would open in spring.
He spent the afternoon listening to old Mexican ballads on the radio.
The recipe calls for a pinch of Mexican oregano, not the Mediterranean kind.
A Mexican wolf was spotted on a trail camera in the national forest.
The film won praise for its portrait of a Mexican family in Los Angeles.
quiet: Исследователи из России, Венгрии, Германии, США, Фран
We ordered Thai food for the whole office on Friday.
Her grandmother was from Mexico and taught her to make tamales from scratch.
The museum opened a new wing devoted to Canadian painters of the 1930s.
The Swedish government announced the new border crossing would open in spring.
He spent the afternoon listening to old Japanese ballads on the radio.
The recipe calls for a pinch of dried oregano, not the fresh kind.
A gray wolf was spotted on a trail camera in the national forest.

predictions: Mexican fire items should all pass; the Russian country-list item in the quiet set will likely fire (~0.6) and cost a near miss; expect hold or marginal.
